newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil recoups early losses.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil recoups early losses.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps recovered their early losses but sentiment remained bearish on concerns of a prompt physical overhang amid weaker overnight crude, traders said on Friday.
"The gas oil outlook is bearish but the swaps market is being held up by paper players who are trading on technicals," one trader said.
September was last quoted unchanged from Thursday at $23.30/$23.40 per barrel, brokers said. It traded in the morning at $23.25, and in the afternoon at $23.33 and $23.35, they said.
October was also unchanged, maintaining the September/October spread at minus 60 cents. October traded this morning at $23.95, they said.

Traders said the steep contango is still making it worthwhile for oil companies to store their gas oil and jet fuel for winter. But the current poor demand is forcing some to sell at big discounts in order to make room for fresh cargoes.
In the physical market, a total of five companies offered gas oil and jet fuel cargoes on Thursday.
Early September gas oil were offered down to a low of $22.60 or at 30 cents below Singapore spot quotes, with no buyers taking them out.
Jet fuel is also under pressure with the regrade slipping due to increasing concerns over high jet fuel stocks.
The September regrade was last quoted at 75/95 cents, down from Thursday's $0.90/$1.10, brokers said.
Fuel oil swaps also came under some selling pressure after baulking the downward trend this morning.
September fuel oil swaps were last quoted unchanged at $104.50/$105.050 per tonne.
